subject_session: 117 sessions across 15 rats (e.g. sub-11265/ses-16030604 for demo figures); 615 units

headline_stat.name: significant grid cells (shuffle p<0.05); median grid score

stated_limitation: the NWB position metadata says "meters" but the values are centimeters (the 1.5 m box spans +/-75); the analysis treats them as cm.

justification.dataset: DANDI 000582 (Sargolini/Moser MEC) is the canonical grid-cell dataset, exactly what an expert would choose.
justification.handling: Real data streamed via remfile, running-epoch and speed filtering, correct cm handling, 200-spike minimum, and layer/tetrode annotations all applied explicitly.
justification.analysis: Standard opexebo grid-score + spatial-autocorrelation pipeline with a proper circular time-shift shuffle null, but the 226 candidate p-values carry no multiple-comparisons correction (harmless here given the massive separation, so not decisive).
justification.correctness: Every headline number (189 significant, median gs 0.93/max 1.44, spacing 58 cm IQR 47-70, layer fractions 41/44/17/21%) reproduces exactly from grid_scores.csv and is internally consistent and physically plausible.
justification.figures: Autocorrelations show unambiguous hexagonal structure, axes are labeled with units, sample sizes are given, and examples are ranked by grid score (the effect measure itself), not an unrelated criterion.
justification.honesty: Claims are proportionate and figures support them; examples are genuinely the strongest grid cells, and one real data caveat (cm vs meters) is stated, but the write-up presents a genuinely clean result without naming the missing multiple-comparisons caveat, keeping it at 3.
